metadata.case_name: CHAU TIM KWAI v. HO KEUNG AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_before: Ran a fish stall in Shatin, sole proprietor

injuries.description: Injury to his head; rendered unconscious
source: He sustained an injury to his head in the accident. He was rendered unconscious, and only regained his consciousness once he had been taken to the Prince of Wales Hospital.

manifestations.description: Dizzy spells lasting for an hour or two, occurring as often as once or twice a day
After standing for 10 minutes or so, his thigh starts to hurt
After squatting for 10 minutes or so, pain begins to develop in his thigh and the lower part of his back
After walking for 15 minutes or so, his hip begins to hurt
After sitting for 30 minutes or so, the area around his pelvis begins to ache
Cannot lift his left arm as much as he could before the accident
Can now only pick up relatively heavy objects using both arms (previously could do so with left arm alone)
Cuts on both his ear lobes

treatments_received: The fracture to his shoulder blade was treated "conservatively"
On 4th December 1992, an operation was carried out to fix the fractures to his pelvis, thigh and femoral condyle with screws and interlocking nails
Transferred to the Cheshire Home, Shatin, on 6th January 1993, and discharged on 13th January
Attended the hospital as an out-patient for physiotherapy for several months

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities arising from multiple fractures and head injury; assessed award for pain, suffering and loss of amenities $425,000.00
Closure of plaintiff's fish stall; loss of earnings and inability to continue running his fish stall
